title: Egyptian Koshari
subtitle: Egypt's beloved street food of rice, lentils, pasta, and spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Koshari layers cooked rice, lentils, and pasta under a sharp tomato sauce and a heap of crispy fried onions. It is Egypt's most popular street food and a deeply satisfying bowl in its own right.
sourceNotes: Koshari emerged in Egypt during the 19th century and is now considered the national dish. The combination of rice, lentils, and pasta reflects the influence of Indian, Italian, and Arab culinary traditions on Egyptian cooking.

recipe.batchNotes: Cook each component separately in larger quantities. Store crispy onions at room temperature in an airtight container.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce improves overnight. Cook the lentils and rice ahead; reheat to serve.

content.text: Work through each component in order and you will have everything ready to assemble at the same time.

items.prepNote: small shape such as ditalini or broken spaghetti

content.text: Cook the lentils in well-salted boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes until tender. Drain and set aside.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions until just tender. Drain and keep warm.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
For the crispy onions, heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt.
Fry for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until dark golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
For the sauce, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the same pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, cumin, and chilli flakes.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes until thickened. Stir in the red wine vinegar and season.
Warm the chickpeas in the sauce or separately in a small pan.
To serve, layer rice, lentils, and pasta in each bowl. Spoon over the tomato sauce and chickpeas. Top with a generous pile of crispy onions.

items.symptom: Onions are soft but not crispy.
items.cause: Too much oil or too low a heat.
items.fix: Raise the heat and spread them thinly in the pan.
Boil hard for 5 more minutes, stirring often.

items.cause: The vinegar in the sauce needs balance.
items.fix: Add more vinegar and a good pinch of salt.
